englishTranslation: Pork belly fried with fish sauce
atAGlance: Ba rọi chiên nước mắm is pork belly fried until crisp, then tossed in garlic fish-sauce glaze. It is salty, sticky, crunchy, and built for sharing with rice.
whatItIs: Ba rọi chiên nước mắm is fried pork belly tossed in garlic fish-sauce glaze. It is crisp-edged, salty-sweet, and much richer than grilled lean pork.
howToEnjoy: Eat with rice while the pork is still crisp. Ask for less chili if the glaze is spicy.
howLocalsOrder: Ba rọi chiên nước mắm is pork belly fried until crisp, then coated in a salty-sweet fish-sauce glaze. Ask less spicy early and order rice or pickles to balance the richness.
worthKnowing: Nước mắm means fish sauce; in this dish it becomes a sticky glaze with sugar and garlic. In Vietnamese home and street cooking, pork often gets its identity from caramelized fish sauce, grill smoke, pickles, herbs, or rice-plate sides.
goodToKnow: Nước mắm is fish sauce, but here it becomes a glaze with sugar and garlic. It is not a lime-pepper salt dip or ginger fish sauce on the side.
travelerCaution: Contains pork belly and fish sauce.
